text: {"overall_winner": "B", "qualities": [{"evidence": "Essay B uses correct spelling throughout ('enjoyable', 'activities', 'community', 'competition'), while Essay A has many misspellings like 'wording', 'canning', 'stuiped', 'sneake', 'jsut'", "quality": "Spelling accuracy", "description": "The essay demonstrates consistent, correct spelling of common and content vocabulary."}, {"evidence": "Essay B has complete sentences with proper punctuation and capitalization, e.g., 'People can go to a community pool for people who know how to swim and for people who don't know how to swim.'", "quality": "Sentence structure control", "description": "The essay forms grammatically complete, properly punctuated sentences rather than run-ons or fragments."}, {"evidence": "Essay B uses a clear organizational frame: introduction posing questions, two body paragraphs each with a topic sentence ('One enjoyable way...'), and a conclusion ('Inconclusion...')", "quality": "Paragraph organization", "description": "The essay is structured into distinct paragraphs with topic sentences and a concluding section."}, {"evidence": "Essay B uses standard grammar such as 'it's gonna cost some money but its worth it' and 'when their active' — though imperfect, it shows more standard usage than Essay A's 'they gonna ask', 'you ain't gonna', 'them made a curfew'", "quality": "Grammatical control", "description": "The essay shows greater command of standard English grammar and pronoun/verb agreement."}, {"evidence": "Essay B maintains a consistent formal register and stays on topic throughout, whereas Essay A shifts into emotional direct address with ALL CAPS and exclamations", "quality": "Register consistency", "description": "The essay sustains a measured, expository tone appropriate to the writing task."}]}
